title: 1974: explaining the Chautauqua to Red Callender
summary: Howard explains Chautauquas as park band concerts of classical pieces and marches.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So what happened after that? Did you feel that you had to learn to play blues like you should have played, or just what did you feel? Did you feel you were too classical, or what?
I had too much classic education.
And you wanted more of the --
What I used to do was play Chattaugua, you know? Do you know what a Chattaugua is?
I've heard the name, but can you explain it? That'll help me.
Well, yeah. Do you know what a Chattagua is, Red?
No, I frankly don't. I've heard the name, but --
Well, in the east -- you know, like we've got bands that play in parks here now?
Yeah.
Well, that's what it is. You go to different parks all around.
And you played march music?
I played march. I played all those classics. You played classics mostly. You didn't have any popular music because nobody had written anything.
And that was called a Chattaugua.
Chattauguas. And that's what the people
would play, you'd play all the classics you could think of. Mama? Oh, I thought you couldn't get in.
I thought I'd open this door so you could have more air.
So -- let's see, I had another question, too. So after that --
Wait a minute. We was on Chattasquas.
Chattasquas

I want to get back to these Chattasquas to explain it so people understand what it is. They had all kinds of instruments there but it wasn't nothing but classics, and you played it and it had directors and so forth, it had a director and all like that. And that's what I played. Now, I played all those trumpet solos that most all the classic men played?
Uh-huh.
